nodes.natural_language: We restate the theorem as the target claim to prove.
nodes.statement: For any positive real numbers a and b, (a+b)^4 \le 8(a^4 + b^4).

nodes.natural_language: (a^2+b^2)^2 \le 2(a^4+b^4) holds for all real a,b, whence the desired bound follows by composing the two quadratic inequalities.
nodes.statement: (a^2 + b^2)^2 \le 2(a^4 + b^4) for all real a, b
(a + b)^2 \le 2(a^2 + b^2) for all real a, b

nodes.natural_language: Squaring the first bound and substituting the second yields (a+b)^4\le[2(a^{2}+b^{2})]^{2}=4(a^{2}+b^{2})^{2}\le8(a^{4}+b^{4}).
nodes.statement: (a + b)^4 \le 8(a^4 + b^4) for all real a, b

nodes.natural_language: (a+b)^2 \le 2(a^2+b^2) holds for all real a,b (by expanding or by AM-GM on a^2,b^2).
nodes.statement: (a + b)^2 \le 2(a^2 + b^2) for all real a, b

nodes.natural_language: (a^2+b^2)^2 \le 2(a^4+b^4) holds for all real a,b, whence the desired bound follows by composing the two quadratic inequalities.
nodes.statement: (a + b)^4 \le 8(a^4 + b^4) for all real a, b
